prompt: Stage 3-1, level 5. You just combined a bow and a sword into a completed damage item. On the board: a 2-star tank with a defensive item, a 2-star bruiser beside it, a 2-star ranged carry at the back and a support behind the tank. Who holds the damage item?
explanation:
A damage item multiplies the attacks of whoever holds it, so it goes on the champion whose attacks are your damage: the ranged carry in the back, who fights from the first second to the last. The bruiser is tempting because it is 2-star and 'in the fight', but front-row units spend the fight being hit and die first, and a damage item on a dead unit does nothing.

The tank already has its defensive item; a sword on it makes neither a better tank nor a real damage dealer. Damage items go where the damage comes from.
principle: Damage items on the damage dealer, and the damage dealer is the one who survives to keep attacking.
commonMistake: Putting the damage item on the front-row unit because it is 'in the fight' and the carry looks fragile.
hint: Ask which champion will still be attacking thirty seconds into the fight, and whose attacks you need to be bigger.
